## New capabilities

- **Routing:** inspect principal bus outputs and reassign mono Audio tracks between supported mono/stereo buses, with identity, code and Pan-state checks.
- **Track Volume:** read, replace or merge verified mono/stereo envelopes, with one Volume lane per track rather than per channel playlist.
- **Pan:** read/write static mono/stereo Pan and replace supported mono or selected stereo-channel automation envelopes.
- **Audio editing:** delete supported timeline placements, trim compact virtual clips in place and retain selected absolute sample ranges as named fragments.
- **Native audio import:** append a full native mono 24-bit / 48 kHz WAV to an existing compatible session using an explicit parent prototype.
- **Markers:** delete supported legacy point markers, add UTF-8 comments and read comments through the opt-in reader.
- **AAF-derived playlists:** read verified anonymous or mixed named/anonymous mono playlists and explicitly materialize missing names from corroborated Audio identities.
- **Format coverage:** 25 fps non-drop timecode conversion, verified long fade-out reading and compact virtual-clip reading.

## Fixes and reliability

- Protect main-playlist counters from being mistaken for block headers, including the 90-playlist edge case.
- Keep automation associated with the correct Audio track in mixed mono/stereo sessions.
- Safely edit independent static Clip Gain points in supported mixed dictionaries, preserving neighboring envelopes and isolating shared points.
- Update the legacy marker-ruler population flag, allowing direct Import Session Data of API-created markers without first resaving the source in Pro Tools.
- Allow supported Pan curves on other tracks when reading or editing a static target, without flattening those curves.
- Strengthen complete prevalidation, reference/pointer preservation and refusal of ambiguous or unsupported layouts.

## Validation and documentation

- **638 tests pass with the local reference corpus.** Private native fixtures are optional; missing fixtures are explicitly skipped, not reported as native validation.
- Supported writing profiles were checked through native comparisons and Pro Tools Ultimate 2024.3.1 opening/playback/saving/reopening where applicable. Native resaves are covered by exact API cycles.
- A Windows/Linux CI workflow for Python 3.8, 3.11 and 3.13 includes regression tests and package checks. This announces the configured workflow, not an already-completed remote matrix run.
- The README has been rebuilt around release highlights, a complete public-capability table and explicit limits. Technical specifications, architecture and handoff are updated.

## Scope and compatibility

This remains a **profile-based, template-driven API**, not a universal PTX editor. Reading a session does not imply every editing operation is supported. Existing historical methods retain their own contracts; new methods do not silently broaden them.

Track creation and general populated-track deletion, AAF/ZIP/CSV processing, MXF editing and unverified modern marker/media layouts remain outside this release. PCM24 append-import and float32 session building are separate profiles with their own metadata, frame-rate and field-width requirements. Unknown structures and overflows are rejected rather than guessed.

Python 3.8+; no third-party runtime dependencies. The current source distribution is **LGPL-2.1-or-later**; see LICENSE, COPYING and NOTICE.md. Attribution and this release do not certify that the separate provenance review or copyright complaint is resolved.

pt_api is an unofficial reverse-engineering interoperability project, without official Avid PTX-format documentation or Avid affiliation. Keep backups and validate edited sessions before production use.
